methodology.note: Runtime triggers are oracle-free. Every artifact's runtime_trigger may consume only information available to a deployed agent (issue text, its own trajectory, the repo working tree); gold patches, gold file lists, and benchmark-private gating-test lists are diagnostic-side only (diagnostic_signature). methodology.note: Composed guardrails carry interaction costs. Instruction-following degrades with constraint density, even self-evident constraints reduce task performance, and agents facing irreconcilable composed constraints fabricate obstacles or disengage. Install bundles (one artifact per hook event, ordered condition branches), not 22 independent gates; every guardrail carries a contract (max_triggers + escape_hatch) so no gate can deadlock a run into budget exhaustion. Composition costs on SWE-bench specifically are unmeasured in the literature — treat bundle design as heuristic pending the Tier-B pilot.

methodology.note: Calibration RRs are observational, not causal. The solved-vs-failed prevalence contrasts that gate promotion (e.g. solved_unrelated_problem RR 7.95) are unadjusted for task difficulty, and behavior-outcome correlations on SWE-bench are known to reverse under difficulty control; interventional testing refutes a large fraction of log-derived failure hypotheses. RRs justify DIAGNOSTIC value (this signature marks failed runs); countermeasure EFFICACY claims require the Tier-B interventional loop. The converse also holds: a behavior whose absence doesn't discriminate (reproduce-first, RR 0.83-0.95) can still help when enforced. Difficulty-stratified re-calibration is recorded future work.

references.authors: Shaokun Zhang, Ming Yin, Jieyu Zhang, Jiale Liu, Zhiguang Han, Jingyang Zhang, Beibin Li, Chi Wang, Huazheng Wang, Yiran Chen, Qingyun Wu

methodology.note: Judge-grounded entries are completeness-role. The eight entries grounding on the llm_judge signal exist so every produced error type has a remedy; the judge layer itself measures near-noise here (cross-model κ≈0 pro-vs-flash, FP 2.04% on 1,815 solved controls — see data/reports) and automated failure attribution is far from ground truth in the literature. Filter to objective-signal entries (catalog_role 'core') when selecting interventions to pilot.

references.title: JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Judges
references.authors: Sijun Tan, Siyuan Zhuang, Kyle Montgomery, William Y. Tang, Alejandro Cuadron, Chenguang Wang, Raluca Ada Popa, Ion Stoica
references.supports: Strong LLM judges are near chance when judging objective correctness (including code) rather than human preference.
references.evidence: On challenging response pairs spanning knowledge, reasoning, math, and coding, many strong models (e.g. GPT-4o) perform just slightly better than random guessing (abstract).

references.title: Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures
references.authors: Harsh Raj, Vipul Gupta, Anas Mahmoud, Razvan-Gabriel Dumitru, Darvin Yi, Aakash Sabharwal, Yunzhong He
references.supports: Independent replication of the judge-tier reliability gap: even frontier judges recover coarse category labels far better than fine-grained failure-mode labels, and ensemble precision is bought only with abstention — supporting the rule to filter judge-grounded entries out of pilot selection.
references.evidence: Strongest of four frontier judges reaches Cohen's κ=0.76 / accuracy 0.80 on category labels (interaction edge + fault side) but accuracy 0.72 / macro-F1 0.64 at failure-mode granularity on 40 worked examples; 4-of-4 selective voting lifts category precision to 0.96 only at 68% coverage (Tables 2–4, §6). Authors: the framework 'may be difficult to deploy in production because judge accuracy remains limited, especially for failure-mode labels' (Limitations).

methodology.note: Verification-layer countermeasures directly surface failures or filter candidates. They may also improve resolution indirectly through repair or candidate selection; this must be measured, not inferred. CONTRIBUTING is an attribution policy and does not constrain intervention endpoints. Current verification entries propose failure_surfacing; a pilot must measure its declared endpoint plus target-fault recurrence, P2P preservation, and cost against baseline and active control. Only scoped experimental evidence can justify an efficacy claim.

references.evidence: Generated tests are an effective filter for proposed code fixes, doubling the precision of SWE-Agent patch selection (abstract).

references.title: Heterogeneous Prompting and Execution Feedback for SWE Issue Test Generation and Selection (e-Otter++)
references.authors: Toufique Ahmed, Jatin Ganhotra, Avraham Shinnar, Martin Hirzel
references.supports: Issue-reproduction test generation whose explicit purpose is detecting whether patches fix the issue — the verification endpoint, independent of any patch generator.
references.evidence: Reaches a fail-to-pass rate of 63% on TDD-Bench Verified — tests that fail pre-patch and pass post-patch, i.e. that detect the failure (abstract).

methodology.note: Scout-to-catalog ingestion path. Novel failure modes surfaced by the scout's consolidation pass (data/discovery) enter the catalog only via the same discipline as every promoted type: an objective anchor, solved-vs-failed cohort calibration, and the full promotion chain (taxonomy + detector + evidence chain + audit + catalog entry). Modes that calibrate flat stay recorded as signals with their negative result.

A fraction of observed benchmark failures are evaluation artifacts, not agent faults: rigid test oracles reject semantically correct patches over undocumented constraints (spec-oracle gap) or superficial representation differences (strict format/type assertions). Independent manual analysis on SWE-bench Verified attributes 16.5% of failed attempts (40/243) to these two modes, with causal confirmation (exposing the hidden constraint flips the task to solved). Implication for this catalog: the blamed fault mass carries an unquantified harness-rigidity component — a failed case whose patch is near-gold and whose own verification was green may be a benchmark artifact rather than an agent error (see the benchmark-artifact annex). Note the mirror-image caveat: such constraint-exposure interventions are oracle-informed when task-specific (they consume knowledge of the hidden test), so only their generic, oracle-free forms are deployable (METH-ORACLE-1).

operational_annex.summary: Context/step-budget management: compaction, pruning, and checkpointing for long-horizon runs

strategies: Compact or prune trajectory history before the context window forces termination — summarize observations, evict stale file contents, keep the plan and the last failing-test state verbatim.
Checkpoint progress (plan, edited files, last test result) so a continuation run can resume instead of restarting.

operational_annex.mechanism: truncated_run marks runs that end mid-action on an exhausted context or step budget. It is not a blamed fault (no capability failed — the run was killed), but it is a first-class operational failure: it ends runs before repair can happen AND suppresses fault detection downstream (the killed-vs-gave-up rule masks tool_failure_not_retried, repair_not_reverified, no_test_after_final_edit and gave_up_early on truncated runs). Compaction directly extends the effective horizon, and published results show it can IMPROVE resolve rates while cutting tokens — so reducing truncation both recovers failed runs and raises diagnosis coverage. Prevalence quantification in the literature is absent; source it from this project's own truncated_run counts.

grounds.patch_condition: agent patch's added-line content (normalized) covers >= 0.7 of the gold patch's added source lines
grounds.suspect_signature: outcome failed AND agent ran tests AND its last test run was green AND the final patch is near-gold by added-line content — the agent's own verification accepted a patch materially matching the reference, yet the harness rejected it

benchmark_artifact_annex.summary: Harness-rigidity triage queue: failed cases whose near-gold patch passed the agent's own verification are benchmark-artifact suspects, not automatically agent faults
benchmark_artifact_annex.mechanism: Rigid test oracles reject semantically correct patches over undocumented constraints or superficial representation differences (METH-HARNESS-1). Such cases contaminate blamed fault mass: the diagnosis layer, which conditions on outcome==failed, will attribute an agent error where the breakdown may be evaluation-side. The suspect signature is deliberately conservative (own verification green + near-gold content) and marks cases for MANUAL review — mirroring the harness-diagnosis step of the source study, where semantic correctness is confirmed by human reviewers, never auto-asserted. Suspects are NOT removed from fault counts; the annex quantifies the confound instead of silently editing the data.
benchmark_artifact_annex.remedy: Evaluation-side, not agent-side: review suspects against the official test_patch (FAIL_TO_PASS assertions) to classify spec-oracle gap vs strict format mismatch vs genuine near-miss; report the confirmed artifact rate alongside headline fault counts.

prevalence.note: Computed over the ARGUS cohort (5 agents x 500 SWE-bench Verified; scripts/harness_suspects.py). ~3.2% of failed cases at the 0.7 threshold — a conservative lower bound vs the 16.5% manual estimate of the source study (content-level near-match misses V2-style representation mismatches, e.g. str vs int, by construction).
